limitations_and_boundaries: The optimization problem is nonconvex and can only be solved to stationarity.
The framework relies on a nonconvex optimization problem, and at best can be solved to stationarity.
NOTEARS-Sob performance degrades when the ground truth is not an additive model.
The kernel-based approach (GSGES) has O(n^3) time complexity, compared to linear dependency on n in NOTEARS-MLP and NOTEARS-Sob.
Hyperparameter tuning is not the main focus; a fixed reasonable λ is used for all settings.

evidence_spans.content: Unlike existing approaches that require specific modeling choices, loss functions, or algorithms, we present a completely general framework that can be applied to general nonlinear models (e.g. without additive noise), general differentiable loss functions, and generic black-box optimization routines.

evidence_spans.content: We develop a framework for learning sparse nonparametric directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) from data. Our approach is based on a recent algebraic characterization of DAGs that led to a fully continuous program for score-based learning of DAG models parametrized by a linear structural equation model (SEM). We extend this algebraic characterization to nonparametric SEM by leveraging nonparametric sparsity based on partial derivatives, resulting in a continuous optimization problem that can be applied to a variety of nonparametric and semiparametric models including GLMs, additive noise models, and index models as special cases.

provenance.text_excerpt: We develop a framework for learning sparse nonparametric directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) from data. Our approach is based on a recent algebraic characterization of DAGs that led to a fully continuous program for score-based learning of DAG models parametrized by a linear structural equation model (SEM). We extend this algebraic characterization to nonparametric SEM by leveraging nonparametric sparsity based on partial derivatives, resulting in a continuous optimization problem that can be applied to a variety of nonparametric and semiparametric models including GLMs, additive noise models, and index models as special cases.

experiments_or_tasks: Apply the framework to various nonparametric and semiparametric models including GLMs, additive noise models, and index models.
Develop a generic optimization problem for learning sparse nonparametric DAGs based on an algebraic characterization of acyclicity extended via partial derivatives.
Evaluate the framework on synthetic data with different graph types and data generating mechanisms, and on a real protein signaling dataset.

methods.name: NOTEARS-MLP
methods.protocol_description: Nonparametric DAG learning using a multilayer perceptron (MLP) with one hidden layer of 10 hidden units and sigmoid activation, trained via augmented Lagrangian and L-BFGS-B to minimize a loss with l1 penalty and acyclicity constraint.

methods.name: NOTEARS-Sob
methods.protocol_description: Nonparametric DAG learning using Sobolev basis expansions with basis functions 'r(u)=sr sin(u/sr), sr=2/((2r-1)π) for r=1,...,10, trained via augmented Lagrangian and L-BFGS-B with l1 penalty and acyclicity constraint.

methods.name: NOTEARS (Linear)
methods.protocol_description: Linear SEM DAG learning method from Zheng et al. (2018) used as a baseline.

methods.name: CAM
methods.protocol_description: Causal additive models method from Bühlmann et al. (2014) used as a baseline.

methods.name: GSGES
methods.protocol_description: Greedy equivalence search with generalized scores from Huang et al. (2018) used as a baseline.

methods.name: DAG-GNN (GNN)
methods.protocol_description: Graph neural network-based DAG learning method from Yu et al. (2019) used as a baseline.

methods.name: FGS
methods.protocol_description: Fast greedy equivalence search from Ramsey et al. (2017) used as a baseline.
